chunks: Ibrahim ibn Salma narrated from Ahmad ibn Malik al-Fazari from Haydar ibn Muhammad al-Fazari from Abbad ibn Yaqub from Nasr ibn Muzahim from Muhammad ibn Marwan from al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
“And in the heaven is your sustenance and what you are threatened with…”
He said: “It is the emergence of the Mahdi (peace be upon him).”
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'And in the heaven is your sustenance' refer to according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* offers a distinctive eschatological tafsir of Surah Adh-Dhariyat, interpreting 'your sustenance' as the arrival of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) rather than material provision. By linking divine promise directly to the Mahdi’s emergence, it underscores the Shia belief that his reappearance constitutes the ultimate fulfillment of God’s covenant and the primary source of spiritual and worldly benefit for humanity.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 130 - The following verses of Quran prove that the rise of Imam Mahdi (a.s) is definite in this Ummah: It is narrated from Ibrahim bin Salma from Ahmad bin Malik Fuzari from Haider bin Muhammad Fuzari from Abbad bin Yaqub from Nasr bin Muzahim from Muhammad bin Marwan from Kulaini from Abi Salih from Ibn Abbas with regard to the verse:
“And in the heaven is your sustenance and what you are threatened with…” (51:22-23)
He said “It implies the rise of the Qaim of Aale Muhammad (a.s).”
